newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall on Yeltsin operation news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall on Yeltsin operation news.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell on news President Boris Yeltsin agreed to have a heart operation, but dealers said the drop was not likely to last long on hopes the operation will be successful.
Yeltsin's spokesman confirmed the Kremlin leader would have heart operation, probably at the end of September, in Moscow.
"Bids disappeared from the market right after the news," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said.
Dealers said the market became more active after a day of mostly calm, range trade, in which prices had earlier edged up.
"It is quite normal there is panic selling. Such operations are surely dangerous, but it is better to have such an operation than to live in a poor condition," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said.
Dealers said uncertainty was likely to remain on the market until the result of the operation is known.
"The news is not so bad in the long term... There may be a catchup if we see Mr Yeltsin in a better shape afterwards. I do not know anybody who died after this kind of operation," Coursault said.
